facts.fact: In 1886 a door-to-door bookseller, David McConnell, gave free perfume samples; customers preferred the perfume, and he founded the California Perfume Company, later Avon.
Harley-Davidson launched the Harley Owners Group (H.O.G.) on January 1, 1983.
On New Year's Eve 1985 Harley-Davidson was hours from filing for bankruptcy before a refinancing deal was signed.
facts.caution: Do not say the club alone saved the company.

facts.fact: Milgram, Bickman & Berkowitz (1969): with 1 person looking up at an empty window, 4% of passers-by stopped; with 15, 40% stopped and 86% looked up.
sources: Journal of Personality and Social Psychology, 1969
facts.caution: A 2012 replication found a weaker effect; cite the original study only.

facts.fact: In 1951 Tupperware left stores and sold only through home parties; sales took off.
In 1518 in Strasbourg, people danced in the streets for weeks (the dancing plague).
sources: Historical record; crowd sizes are disputed
facts.caution: Say 'hundreds' or 'dozens', never an exact number.

facts.fact: H.O.G. launched January 1, 1983. The first membership pack had a pin, a patch, a membership card and a Touring Handbook; rallies followed (first event: 250 members). Today it has close to a million members and about 1,500 chapters.
facts.caution: Do not say the club alone saved the company (see harley-1985).

facts.fact: Kurt Lewin noticed a waiter remembered unpaid orders better than paid ones. Bluma Zeigarnik (1927) gave 32 adults 22 tasks and interrupted some: interrupted tasks were recalled about 90% better on average (IR/CR = 1.9).
facts.caution: Later replications are mixed; cite the original study only.

facts.fact: At a Tupperware party the dealer looked for guests willing to host future parties; hostesses received merchandise as a thank-you, and hostesses and guests were often recruited as dealers.

Dropbox's referral program gave both the inviter and the invited friend extra storage. Drew Houston (Startup Lessons Learned, 2010) said it permanently increased signups by 60%; users sent 2.8 million direct referral invites in April 2010.

Clark et al. (University of Cambridge, Neuron 2009): on a simplified slot machine, near-misses felt less pleasant than full misses but increased the desire to keep playing, and recruited the same striatal and insula circuitry that responded to wins.
facts.caution: Say 'almost winning lights up the same brain circuits as winning' and 'makes people want to keep playing'. Do not say it causes addiction.
